{{Short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox college sports team season |year=2024–25 |team=Stanford Cardinal |sport=Basketball |image=Stanford Cardinal logo.svg |image_size= 100 |conference=Atlantic Coast Conference |conference_link= Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball |short_conf=ACC |CoachRank= |APRank= |record= 21–14 |conf_record= 11–9 |head_coach=[[Kyle Smith (basketball)|Kyle Smith]] |hc_year=1st |assoc_coach=[[Eric Reveno]] |asst_coach1=Jim Shaw |asst_coach2=Wayne Hunter |asst_coach3=Derrick Wrobel |asst_coach4=Stephen Frankoski |stadium=[[Maples Pavilion]] |champion= |tourney= [[2025 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] |tourney_result= Second Round }} {{2024–25 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2024–25 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team''' represented [[Stanford University]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They played their home games at [[Maples Pavilion]]. They were led by first-year head coach [[Kyle Smith (basketball)|Kyle Smith]]. This was the inaugural season for Stanford as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The team started the season well, winning six straight games, a streak which culminated in a 71–69 win at [[2024–25 Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball team|Santa Clara]]. The team then went on a two-game losing streak, losing in the [[Acrisure Holiday Invitational]] to [[2024–25 Grand Canyon Antelopes men's basketball team|Grand Canyon]] and to [[2024–25 Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball team|Cal Poly]]. They rebounded to win three straight games, including a rivalry match and their ACC opener against [[2024–25 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]]. That streak ended as the Cardinal faced their first ranked team of the season in number ten [[2024–25 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]]. They fell at a neutral site in the San Jose Tip-Off 76–61. They then went on their first ACC road trip to the east coast, where they lost to [[2024–25 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] and [[2024–25 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]]. They rebounded from the road trip and went 6–1 over their next seven games, with five of those games being at home. They went 1–1 in the road games, with a loss at [[2024–25 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] and a win at [[2024–25 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. The team stumbled and went 1–4 over their next five games. They only defeated [[2024–25 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] 74–73, while losing to [[2024–25 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]], Wake Forest, [[2024–25 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] and third-ranked [[2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] over the stretch. The Cardinal finished 3–2 over their last five games, winning their three games at home and losing their two games on the road. The stretch included wins over rival California, SMU, and [[2024–25 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]]. The two losses were their final to games of the season versus [[2024–25 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]] and fourteenth-ranked [[2024–25 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]]. The Cardinal finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|season]] 21–14 and 11–9 in [[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in seventh place. As the seventh seed in the [[2025 ACC men's basketball tournament|2025 ACC tournament]] earned a bye into Second Round where they faced rival California for the third time during the season. They continued their dominance over the Golden Bears, defeating them for the third time during the season. They fell advanced to the Quarterfinals where they lost to second seed and thirteenth ranked Louisville for the second time in six days, 75–73. They received an [[2025 National Invitation Tournament#At-large bids|at-large]] bid to the [[2025 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]]. The Cardinal were a two-seed in the San Francisco Region. They defeated [[2024–25 Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball team|Cal State Northridge]] in the First Round before losing to [[2024–25 Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball team|Kent State]] 77–75 in the Second Round. ==Previous season== The [[2023–24 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Cardinal]] went 14–18, 8–12 in the Pac-12 conference. They finished tied for 9th in the conference and, as the 10th seed, played [[2023–24 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] in the first round of the [[2024 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 Conference tournament]]. The Cardinal beat the Golden Bears 87–76 in overtime and faced their next head coach and the second seed, [[2023–24 Washington State Cougars men's basketball team|Washington State]]. The Cardinal lost to the Cougars 79–62, ending their season. After the game, the Cardinal fired their head coach [[Jerod Haase]] after eight seasons and zero appearances in the NCAA tournament.{{Cite web |date=March 14, 2024|title=Stanford fires coach Jerod
